title: What You See is What You Get: Exploiting Visibility for 3D Object Detection

problem.summary: Many contemporary deep networks process 3D point clouds, making it hard to distinguish the two regions (left). Recent advances in 3D sensing have created unique challenges for computer vision.
statements: Many contemporary deep networks process 3D point clouds, making it hard to distinguish the two regions (left).
Recent advances in 3D sensing have created unique challenges for computer vision.
One fundamental challenge is finding a good representation for 3D sensor data.
While this is a fundamental challenge in machine vision dating back to stereoscopic processing, it has recently been explored in the context of deep neural processing of 3D sensors such as LiDARs.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we introduce deep 3D networks that leverage freespace to significantly improve 3D object detection accuracy.

On the NuScenes 3D detection benchmark, we show that, by adding an additional stream for visibility input, we can significantly improve the overall detection accuracy of a state-of-the-art 3D detector.
In this paper, we demonstrate such knowledge can be efficiently recovered through 3D raycasting and readily incorporated into batch-based gradient learning.

Despite the popularity, such visibility reasoning has not been widely studied in the context of object detection, except a notable exception of [34], which develops a probabilistic framework based on occupancy maps to detect objects with known surface models.
